evidence_of_progress.note: Adjusted operating margin: Q2 FY26 expanded 80 bps (Kuehneman, doc 173066, 2026-05-28); Q3 FY26 9.0%, up 60 bps (Kuehneman, doc 200250, 2026-08-27); first nine months up 30 bps (Ghingo, doc 200250). FY26 adjusted EPS guide raised and narrowed to $1.45-$1.51 while organic sales guide cut to 1%-2%. No margin level or bps target has been issued by the new team; the only numeric framing is the 2%-3% sales and 5%-7% earnings growth algorithm and restructuring gross savings of 2x to 3x a $20M-$25M cost. The legacy Transform and Modernize target ($250M+ operating income by end FY2026) dates from the October 2023 Investor Day under the prior CEO and is outside the window. Margin is partly commodity driven (pork trim, beef, bellies, turkey); management divested whole-bird turkey to reduce that exposure.

verdict: Cheap, de-rated and with flat estimates, but the CEO is an internal promotion and the new team has offered only a growth algorithm, not a numeric margin target, so the GXO-style gap between management framing and consensus does not yet exist.
open_questions: Will Ghingo (CEO from 2026-10-26) and new CFO Bhumbla set a margin target or Investor Day with the FY2026 Q4 results in December?
How much of the 30-80 bps adjusted margin gains is commodity relief versus restructuring and portfolio pruning?
What replaces Transform and Modernize after FY2026, and was its $250M+ operating income target met?
